subject: Split billing for Aurora pilot — per-seat allocation + EU VAT reverse-charge (POs / remit)
content:
From: Lucia Garcia <lucia.garcia@aurora-health.eu>
To: Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood.ai>
Cc: Tom Henderson <tom.henderson@aurora-health.eu>
Date: Fri, 07 Aug 2027 09:12:00 +0200
Subject: Split billing request for pilot — per-seat split + VAT reverse-charge

Hi Sofia,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday — the pilot looks promising and the procurement team wants to move forward. Before we issue the POs, finance asked for a split-invoice approach so we can allocate costs to two Aurora legal entities and handle VAT correctly for EU operations. Quick details below: 

- Requirement: Issue two invoice lines (or two invoices) so EU consumption is billed to Aurora NL (EU legal entity) and US consumption to Aurora US (US legal entity).
- VAT: For the EU portion we intend to apply reverse-charge (Aurora NL will self-account).
- Cost centers / POs: We will provide separate PO numbers for each cost center and need those PO numbers to be reflected on the invoice lines for internal chargeback.
- Billing cadence: Monthly, with net 30.

Attached are the draft POs for the two cost centers for the initial month (Aurora_PO_4312.pdf, Aurora_PO_4313.pdf). Can Redwood issue invoices with separate remit-to details for each legal entity and include the VAT reverse-charge note on the EU line? Also, do you support separate electronic remittances (i.e., two distinct bank instructions on one statement) or do you prefer two standalone invoices?

Appreciate guidance — cc'ing Tom (procurement).

Best,
Lucia
Finance Manager | Aurora Health Systems
attachments: Aurora_PO_4312.pdf (application/pdf), Aurora_PO_4313.pdf (application/pdf)

---

From: Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood.ai>
To: Lucia Garcia <lucia.garcia@aurora-health.eu>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 07 Aug 2027 10:03:00 +0200
Subject: Re: Split billing request for pilot — per-seat split + VAT reverse-charge

Hi Lucia — thanks for the POs and clear ask. Looping in Rishi (billing ops) and Kimberly (finance) so we can confirm the right invoicing pattern. A few quick questions to help us map this exactly: 

1) Can you confirm the legal-entity billing details (legal name, address, VAT/tax ID) for Aurora NL and Aurora US as you want them shown on the invoices?
2) Do you want us to send: (A) one consolidated statement with two invoice line items (each tagged to a different legal entity) and a combined payment instruction that lists two remit options; or (B) two separate invoice documents (one per legal entity) with independent remit instructions?
3) Please share the final cost_center codes you want printed on the invoice lines (these will be added to the invoice 'PO / Cost center' column).

We typically handle reverse-charge by including the customer's VAT ID and the following note on the EU invoice line: 'VAT reverse charge — customer liable for VAT under Article 194(1) EU VAT Directive' and zero-rate the VAT amount. If you need a specific phrasing for audit in NL, paste it into a reply and we'll copy it verbatim.

I've attached a short template (redwood-split-template.xlsx) that shows how we can render the two-line split on a single invoice versus two invoices. Once we have the legal names and VAT IDs we'll draft the invoice(s) and share for confirmation.

Best,
Sofia Ivanova
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
attachments: redwood-split-template.xlsx (application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.spreadsheetml.sheet)

---

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood.ai>
Cc: Lucia Garcia <lucia.garcia@aurora-health.eu>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 07 Aug 2027 11:28:00 +0200
Subject: Re: Split billing request for pilot — per-seat split + VAT reverse-charge

Hi all,

We can support both options but there are trade-offs: 

Option A — Single PDF invoice with two discrete lines (tagged to different legal entities):
- Pros: single document for the client; easier in our AR system for consolidated reporting.
- Cons: many ERPs require separate remit-to/bank instructions per legal-entity — that can confuse payment processing unless both remits are clearly delineated and accepted by the payer.

Option B — Two separate invoices (one per legal entity):
- Pros: clean legal mapping, unambiguous remit instructions, simpler for chargeback.
- Cons: two invoice numbers and two payment expectations; requires Aurora to either send two payments or do internal reallocation.

For EU reverse-charge we need the customer's VAT number on the invoice and will zero-rate VAT on the EU invoice lines. We will include this standard note: 'Transaction subject to reverse charge; recipient to account for VAT.' If Aurora prefers a specific statutory citation for NL, we can insert it.

If you choose Option B we will:
- Issue Invoice RED-2027-0457 to Aurora Health Systems NL (VAT ID: NL123456789B01) for the EU seat allocation, VAT 0.00 with reverse-charge note.
- Issue Invoice RED-2027-0458 to Aurora Health Systems US for the US seat allocation, standard tax treatment (if any).

Please confirm the two legal-entity billing blocks below and the final PO/cost-center codes so we can create draft invoices: 
- Aurora Health Systems NL | VAT: ______ | Legal address: ______ | PO: PO-4312 | Cost center: CC-EMEA-019
- Aurora Health Systems US | Tax ID: ______ | Legal address: ______ | PO: PO-4313 | Cost center: CC-US-034

Attaching a draft of the split invoice layout for internal review.

Regards,
Rishi Malhotra
Billing Operations | Redwood Inference
attachments: split-invoice-draft.pdf (application/pdf)

Hi Lucia — thanks for the clear details, that works. Next steps from Redwood finance: 

1) We will issue two discrete invoices: RED-2027-0457 (Aurora Health Systems B.V. — NL) and RED-2027-0458 (Aurora Health Systems, Inc. — US).

Thanks,
Kimberly Park
